_comment: Per-unit release lanes (docs/adr/1650-per-unit-control-plane-releases.md). Every release binary (Makefile DAEMONS + CLIS) appears here. lane: control-plane = runs only on the control plane and deploys alone through cd-controlplane's unit lane; edge = the gateways, deployed after the control plane by cd-edge-units.yml one host at a time (services name the host role they run on); shared = also runs on compute hosts, so a change waits for the full release; compute = compute hosts only (and database nodes, ADR-1027: pgproxyd, dbbackupd and vmmd there wait for the full release too); tool = operator/customer CLI, never restarted. pkg/daemonunitspec/release_units_lane_test.go keeps lanes, services and readiness URLs in lockstep with the daemon registry; scripts/ci/affected_units_test.py keeps the binary set in lockstep with the Makefile.

gates._comment: SLO gate per host (scripts/ci/slo_gate.py --duration/--max-hold). The canary is the first host of a lane: the control plane in the control-plane lane, the designated compute node in the edge lane (the control plane when no compute node restarts a gateway). Every later host gets the follower gate, long enough to catch crash loops and immediate error spikes. scripts/ci/plan_edge_rollout.py checks these against the 30-minute budget (ADR-1650).

watch._comment: Post-deploy watch (docs/adr/20261020214632-automatic-unit-deploy-safety-rails.md): the SLO gate keeps running for `window` after a run's last activation, each rule held for its own for: (max hold = window). `max_blind_rounds` rounds without evidence (5 minutes at the interval) make it inconclusive. A host holds at most `max_unwatched` unit releases not yet watched clean, so release retention (3 previous releases) still holds its known-good release.

_migrations_comment: Goose migrations (*.sql directly in migrations_dir). When every one added since base is lane-eligible (declared -- migration-compat: expand, no contract change; docs/adr/20261018084150-unit-lane-expand-migrations.md), they are the data step the control-plane lane applies before restarting anything. Otherwise they block like any other path under blocking_paths.migrations.
_host_config_comment: Host configuration (docs/adr/20261018133100-host-configuration-lane.md). A deploy/ path a control-plane host role reads (scripts/ci/host_roles.py: the role's files and every path it names) no longer blocks the control-plane lane, which converges the roles whose content hash changed before it restarts anything (cd-controlplane.yml converge-host-config). A path a compute host role reads waits for the full release and holds the edge lane (compute_deploy). release_units are the files cd-controlplane's bundle installs through deployctl at activation (systemd/, optional-systemd/, tmpfiles.d/): a unit release reuses the base's copies, so a change to one still needs a full release. stateful_services are services the lane never restarts: a role that can restart or stop one (a task, or a notified handler of any role, scripts/ci/host_roles.py restart_roles) blocks both lanes when its content changes (stateful_restart), the planner never selects it on its own, and in lane mode the roles refuse a restart (faas_stateful_restart_allowed). outside_releases are trees no release installs, so a change there maps to nothing unless a host role names the file: deploy/systemd/ is deployctl generate's legacy and dev-VM tree, deploy/grafana/ mirrors the grafana role's dashboards (make grafana-mirror-check), and deploy/cloudflare/ workers deploy through their own workflows.
